routerChecklistIsolation: Turn OFF "AP isolation" / "client isolation" on the router - it blocks devices from seeing each other and breaks pairing.
routerChecklistSameNetwork: Put the mother and every team device on the same network name (not a guest network).
routerChecklistBand: 2.4 GHz reaches further through walls; 5 GHz is faster at shorter range.
firewallHint: If other devices can see this mother but can't connect to it, allow the network port through Windows Firewall. A Windows (UAC) confirmation will appear.
firewallHintChild: If this device can't detect the mother even though it is on the same network, allow network access (mDNS/UDP) through Windows Firewall. A Windows (UAC) confirmation will appear.
firewallOk: Network access allowed. Devices should be able to connect now.
firewallErr: Couldn't allow access (Windows prompt declined?). Try again and accept the confirmation.
revokeConfirm: Remove this device? It will no longer reconnect on its own: to add it back, use "Join" from that device.
satelliteHint: Join a mother on the same network to receive the games launched on it.
discoverEmpty: No mother found. Check that this device is on the same network as the mother, then search again. Still nothing while the mother is on? Restart Playground on the mother, then on this device.
troubleshootSameNetwork: Make sure this device is on the same network (router) as the mother.
troubleshootIsolation: On a router, turn off "AP isolation" / "client isolation" - it hides devices from each other.
troubleshootMotherOpen: Check Playground is open on the mother, on the same network.
joinAlreadyPaired: This device is already paired with {{label}}. Ask the operator to revoke it there first, then try again.
joinUnreachableFirewall: This device can SEE {{label}} but can't connect to it. This is almost always the MOTHER's firewall: on the mother device, open Settings → Network → Advanced and tap “Allow network access” (accept the Windows prompt). If that doesn't help, the mother may have just gone offline.
rejoinDesc: Finds the device currently hosting and points this one at it. Use it when this device lost the game after another device took it over. Changes nothing on the mother.
rejoinDone: Reconnected. The games list and the running game follow the current mother again.
rejoinNotFound: No mother found on the network for this device. Check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi, then try again.
forceMotherTitle: Resume the game on this device
forceMotherDesc: This device hosts the running game in place of the absent mother. If another device already hosts it, its latest state is pulled in first, so nothing is lost. This device hands back to the mother as soon as it returns.
forceMotherDone: This device now hosts the game. Open it to continue: the other devices will reconnect.
forceMotherRestarted: This device hosts its games again. The other devices will reconnect.
diagIntro: Runs a search for mothers and shows this device's mDNS state. Take a screenshot on BOTH the mother and the child.
diagApipaWarning: This device did not get an address from the router (169.254.x address). Check it is really connected to the router network, then reconnect the Wi-Fi or the cable.
diagFirewallMissing: MISSING or outdated (another build of the app) - use "Allow network access" above
relaunchNote: Playground will restart to apply the change.
winHealthOk: This device's Windows settings are fine.
winHealthIssuesTitle: Windows settings to fix on this device
winHealthSleep: Sleep on mains after {{minutes}} min: this device would fall asleep mid-game.
winHealthWifiPower: Windows may turn the Wi-Fi card off to save power.
winHealthPublic: Network on the Public profile ({{names}}): devices may not see each other.
winHealthFixHint: A single Windows permission prompt (UAC) is shown.
mySatellitesHint: The devices connected to this mother.
statusMotherRouterBody: This device is the mother, on the {{ssid}} network. {{count}} satellite(s) are connected.
statusReconnectingBody: This device is reconnecting to the mother on its own. Don't touch anything.
statusSatelliteBody: This device is a satellite, connected to the mother {{mother}} over the {{ssid}} Wi-Fi.
statusLastExchange: Last exchange with the mother {{seconds}} s ago
statusNoMotherOnWifi: This device is a satellite. It is on the {{ssid}} Wi-Fi but can't find a mother.
statusNoMotherNoWifi: This device is a satellite, and it isn't connected to any Wi-Fi.
statusSearchNotFound: Check that the mother is on, that Playground is open on it, and that this device is on the same network. Still nothing? Restart Playground on the mother, then on this device.
myMotherNone: This device isn't linked to any mother.
motherSatellitesHint: The devices connected to the same mother as this one.
motherSatellitesNone: No device is connected to the mother.
motherSatellitesUnavailable: List unavailable: the mother is not responding.
advRoleHintMother: Mother. One per account; change it only to replace the mother.
advRoleHintSatellite: Satellite. Change it only if this device permanently replaces the mother.
advJoinHint: List the mothers on the network and join one
advWindowsHint: Sleep, Wi-Fi card power saving, network profile
advRejoinHint: Re-attach to the game's current mother
advResumeHint: If the mother went down: host the game on this device, as a substitute
roleChoiceToMotherWarn: This device will be the mother at every start, and the former mother will become a satellite. Only do this to replace the mother: there is one per account.
roleChoiceToSatelliteWarn: This device will no longer be the mother. Not possible while it alone hosts a running game.
hotspotRemovedNotice: The mother no longer creates a Wi-Fi hotspot: connect every device to the same router (or network), and install the same Playground version on each of them.
networkCardSub: Every device must be connected to the same router or network, through Windows. Satellites find this mother automatically.
networkCardNoAddress: No network address: connect this PC to the router.
networkCardAddressHint: If a satellite can't find this mother, type this address on the satellite: Settings → Network → Advanced options → Connect by IP address.
routerChecklistMulticast: Allow multicast (mDNS) - otherwise use "Connect by IP address" on the satellites.
byIpHint: If the search can't find the mother (a network that blocks automatic discovery), type its IP address, shown on the mother in Settings → Network.
byIpUnreachable: No mother answers at {{address}}. Check the address, that both devices are on the same network, and the mother's firewall.
advByIpHint: When the automatic search finds nothing
troubleshootByIp: Still nothing? Use "Connect by IP address" with the address shown on the mother.
protoMotherOutdated: {{label}} runs an older Playground version ({{version}}). Update the mother so the devices can talk to each other.
protoSelfOutdated: Update this device: the mother runs a newer Playground version ({{version}}).
updateFromMotherNone: This mother has no update to offer this device. Update it over the internet.
updateFromMotherUnreachable: Couldn't reach this mother for the update.
statusSubstituteBody: This device hosts the games in place of {{mother}}, which is away. It will hand back as soon as {{mother}} returns. {{count}} satellite(s) connected.
statusSubstituteBodyUnknown: This device hosts the games in place of the mother, which is away. It will hand back as soon as the mother returns. {{count}} satellite(s) connected.
statusMotherWaitingBody: {{name}} is hosting a running game in place of this device. This device will take the hosting back as soon as that game is over.
statusMotherStartingBody: No other mother found: this device takes over hosting the games.
statusTwoMothersTitle: Two devices are set as mother
statusTwoMothersBody: This device and {{name}} are both set as mother. There can only be one: choose which to keep.
statusHostAsSubstitute: Host the games as a substitute
statusHostAsSubstituteHint: If the mother is away: this device hosts the games in its place, and hands back as soon as it returns.
statusHostAsSubstituteDone: This device now hosts the games, in place of the mother.
statusRoleResetNote: Since the update, this device is no longer set as mother. If it is your mother device, set it in Advanced options → Role of this device.
networkCardRouterLine: Plug the supplied router into a USB port of this device.
